programs.title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
programs.summary: Bring AI agents, research design, and responsible practice to another field.
rules: The official award is a BA in Interdisciplinary Studies, managed by the Department of Data Science.
At least 120 credits are needed for the overall degree. The 30 hours covers the major, not all graduation requirements.

The PHIL 150 alternative is specifically identified by the program as Philosophy of Technology (4 credits). The generic PHIL 150 course record is First-Year Seminar with variable topics; arbitrary PHIL 150 sections are not verified equivalents.
Choosing the four-credit PHIL 150 topic produces 31 credits with the listed six elective credits.
AAI 101, AAI 301 and AAI 302 have their own catalog course records even though the undergraduate subject index omits an AAI listing; do not silently replace them with DATA 101, DATA 305 or DATA 415.
Course-description prerequisites and corequisites may add credits. If taking CSCI 141, include CSCI 141L (0 credits). If taking MATH 109, include MATH 109L (1 credit).
programs.fit: Use and evaluate AI tools in another field: agent design, coordinated AI workflows, research design, visualization, ethics and trustworthy AI.
notes: DATA 210 and DATA 405 list DATA 101, CSCI 140 or CSCI 141 as prerequisites. Their entries do not list AAI 101; confirm an approved route with the department rather than assuming equivalence.
PHIL 150 must be the Philosophy of Technology topic identified in the program, not an arbitrary first-year seminar. That 4-credit route raises the listed 30-credit minimum to 31.

rules: At least half of the minimum required number of CS major courses must be taken at W&M.
At most two 300/400-level courses taken elsewhere may count toward the CS major.

programs.title: Business Analytics
programs.summary: Connect analytical tools to business decisions, strategy, and organizational challenges.
rules: Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA), not Bachelor of Science.
The 2026–27 curriculum is intended for students matriculating in Fall 2026 or later; earlier students should consult their matriculation-year catalog.
Apply for Business School admission, including for a secondary business major. Admission is competitive.
Before entry: at least 39 earned credits, prerequisite subjects, and at least 2.50 GPA at application and matriculation.
For current W&M students, Business Statistics plus lab and Principles of Accounting must be completed at W&M; transfer credit is not accepted for these admission requirements.
Applications due February 1 for fall admission and September 15 for spring admission; separate transfer process.
Core study usually begins spring of sophomore year or fall of junior year; first semester is a cohort-based Integrated Foundation Semester including analytics, finance and marketing.
For graduation: at least 120 total credits, at least 60 credits outside Mason academic subjects, general education and proficiency requirements, and all core/major requirements.
All BBA students must complete ECON 102 before graduation (explicit on the Data Science BBA page).
Maintain at least 2.0 overall and business-course GPA. Business courses cannot be audited; pass/fail only when the course description specifies it.
Optional second-business-area concentrations are not required, and course availability is not guaranteed.
Only one declared major may be in business; at most eight credits may be shared by two majors under the current program text.
programs.fit: Develop business intelligence, predictive and prescriptive analytics.
notes: Data Science BBA prose says the major requires 12 credits, but its published table lists 9 required credits plus three electives (9 credits) and totals 18. This dataset displays the table and preserves the conflict.

The Data Science BBA core table totals 29 and includes BUAD 330. The Supply Chain BBA core table totals 28 and omits BUAD 330. BUAD course descriptions require BUAD 330 and BUAD 300 as foundation-semester corequisites, while BUAD 300 is absent from both core tables.

Business admission text requires introductory calculus but delegates precise W&M equivalencies to Mason. The catalog course list includes MATH 108, 111 and 131; this dataset does not assert that all three automatically satisfy admission.
